## Overview: Recreating Figure 1e from Wang et al. (*Nature*, 2025)

This standalone R Markdown notebook recreates the **3-panel multimodal validation plot (Figure 1e)** from the reference study (*"Molecular and cellular dynamics of the developing human neocortex"*, Wang et al., *Nature* 2025) directly on your already-processed Multiome Seurat object (`<sample_id>_multiome_merged.rds`), **without** needing to re-run the preprocessing pipeline.

### The Three Molecular Readouts Aligned Across Cell Types:
1. **Left Panel — Gene Expression (snRNA-seq):** Dot plot displaying the **fraction of cells expressing each transcription factor (`%`)** (dot size) and the **min–max normalized (`[0, 1]`) mean RNA expression** within each cell type (viridis fill color).
2. **Middle Panel — Promoter Chromatin Accessibility (snATAC-seq):** Aggregated ATAC-seq fragment coverage tracks (`Signac::CoveragePlot`) centered at the **Transcription Start Site (TSS / promoter window)** of each transcription factor across cell types.
3. **Right Panel — Motif Regulatory Activity (`chromVAR`):** Heatmap displaying the **min–max normalized (`[0, 1]`) mean `chromVAR` motif accessibility score** (`JASPAR2020`) for each transcription factor's binding motif across the genome.

---

## 1. Configure Input Paths & Parameters

Edit the sample ID, input `.rds` path, cell-type metadata column (`"ScType"` or `"Azimuth_cellType"`), and the list of signature Transcription Factors below.

```{r config}
# 1. Sample Identifier
sample_id <- "GG001AC"

# 2. Path to the already-merged Multiome Seurat object (.rds) from test_process_and_merge_atac.Rmd
output_dir <- paste0("./outputs/test_", sample_id)
multiome_rds_path <- file.path(output_dir, paste0(sample_id, "_multiome_merged.rds"))

# Optional fallback if you saved the RDS in another directory:
# multiome_rds_path <- "/path/to/GG001AC_multiome_merged.rds"

# 3. Path to 10x ATAC fragments file (used by CoveragePlot to stream promoter coverage tracks)
fragments_path <- paste0(
  "/data-pure/sequencing/ngs/NGS2026_10893/HG38/count/cellranger/",
  sample_id, "/atac_fragments.tsv.gz"
)

# 4. Which metadata column defines the cell types (rows of Figure 1E)?
# Options: "ScType" (from your RNA object), "Azimuth_cellType", or "seurat_clusters"
preferred_celltype_col <- "ScType"

# 5. Lineage-Defining Transcription Factor Selection Mode
# Set auto_discover_tfs = TRUE to automatically identify the top 10-15 lineage-defining TFs
# specific to your dataset via differential expression across cell types/clusters (intersected
# with JASPAR2020 motifs and ATAC gene annotations).
auto_discover_tfs <- TRUE
target_n_tfs      <- 12   # Target number of lineage-defining TFs to plot (recommended: 10 to 15)
min_target_tfs    <- 10
max_target_tfs    <- 15

# Fallback / manual TF list (used if auto_discover_tfs = FALSE, or as fallback):
# Reference paper Fig. 1e TFs: c("PAX6", "EMX2", "EOMES", "TBR1", "MEF2C", "MAF", "SOX8", "IRF8")
manual_signature_tfs <- c("PAX6", "EMX2", "EOMES", "TBR1", "MEF2C", "MAF", "SOX8", "IRF8")

# Promoter window (+/- bp around the canonical TSS) for the middle panel coverage tracks
promoter_flank_bp <- 1500

cat("Sample ID:          ", sample_id, "\n")
cat("Multiome RDS Path:  ", multiome_rds_path, "\n")
cat("Cell-Type Column:   ", preferred_celltype_col, "\n")
cat("Auto-Discover TFs:  ", auto_discover_tfs, " (Target: ", target_n_tfs, " TFs; range ",
    min_target_tfs, "-", max_target_tfs, ")\n", sep = "")
```

## 2. Load Required Libraries

We load `Seurat`, `Signac`, `JASPAR2020`, `TFBSTools`, and `BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38` (matching [`18_Motif_analysis.R`](file:///Users/franz/Documents/Code/Ganglioglioma/Human_Cortex_Dev_Multiome-main/RScript/18_Motif_analysis.R)), along with `ggplot2`, `patchwork`, `dplyr`, `tidyr`, and `viridis` for assembling the 3-panel figure.

```{r load_libraries}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(Seurat)
  library(Signac)
  library(JASPAR2020)
  library(TFBSTools)
  library(motifmatchr)
  library(chromVAR)
  library(SummarizedExperiment)
  library(BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38)
  library(EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86)
  library(GenomicRanges)
  library(GenomeInfoDb)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(patchwork)
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(viridis)
  library(scales)
})
```

## 3. Load Processed Multiome Object & Verify Cell-Type Grouping

We load the processed `multiome_obj` `.rds` file (automatically preferring the cached `_with_chromvar.rds` if already computed), verify the cell-type annotation column (`ScType` or `Azimuth_cellType`), and ensure the ATAC `Fragment` file pointer is active.

```{r load_object}
chromvar_rds_path <- file.path(output_dir, paste0(sample_id, "_multiome_merged_with_chromvar.rds"))
if (file.exists(chromvar_rds_path)) {
  cat("Found cached Multiome RDS with 'chromvar' assay:", chromvar_rds_path, "\n")
  multiome_obj <- readRDS(chromvar_rds_path)
} else if (file.exists(multiome_rds_path)) {
  cat("Loading processed Multiome Seurat object:", multiome_rds_path, "\n")
  multiome_obj <- readRDS(multiome_rds_path)
} else {
  stop("Processed Multiome RDS file not found at: ", multiome_rds_path,
       "\nPlease check 'multiome_rds_path' in Chunk 1.")
}
cat("Loaded object with", ncol(multiome_obj), "cells and assays:",
    paste(names(multiome_obj@assays), collapse = ", "), "\n")

# Resolve cell-type metadata column (checks preferred_celltype_col first, then fallbacks)
candidate_cols <- unique(c(
  preferred_celltype_col,
  "ScType", "sctype", "SCType",
  "Azimuth_cellType", "seurat_clusters"
))
matched_cols <- intersect(candidate_cols, colnames(multiome_obj@meta.data))

if (length(matched_cols) == 0) {
  stop("None of the candidate cell-type columns were found in multiome_obj@meta.data.")
}
celltype_col <- matched_cols[1]
cat("Using cell-type grouping column:", celltype_col, "\n")

# Clean NA / empty labels and set as active Idents
cell_labels <- as.character(multiome_obj@meta.data[[celltype_col]])
cell_labels[is.na(cell_labels) | cell_labels == ""] <- "Unannotated"
multiome_obj@meta.data[[celltype_col]] <- factor(cell_labels)
Idents(multiome_obj) <- celltype_col

# Establish consistent top-to-bottom cell-type ordering across all 3 panels
celltype_levels <- levels(Idents(multiome_obj))
cat("Cell types (", length(celltype_levels), "):\n", sep = "")
print(table(Idents(multiome_obj)))

# Ensure gene annotations are attached to the ATAC assay
DefaultAssay(multiome_obj) <- "ATAC"
if (is.null(Annotation(multiome_obj)) || length(Annotation(multiome_obj)) == 0) {
  cat("Attaching EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86 (hg38) gene annotations to ATAC assay...\n")
  annotations <- GetGRangesFromEnsDb(ensdb = EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86)
  seqlevelsStyle(annotations) <- "UCSC"
  genome(annotations) <- "hg38"
  Annotation(multiome_obj) <- annotations
}
```

---

## 4. Compute JASPAR2020 Motif Matrix & `chromVAR` Activity (`18_Motif_analysis.R`)

Following [`18_Motif_analysis.R`](file:///Users/franz/Documents/Code/Ganglioglioma/Human_Cortex_Dev_Multiome-main/RScript/18_Motif_analysis.R) and the paper's Methods (*"TF motif enrichment analysis"*, p. 12):
- If the `"chromvar"` assay is not yet present in `multiome_obj`, we filter the ATAC peaks to standard chromosomes (`BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38`), fetch the vertebrate CORE position frequency matrices from `JASPAR2020`, attach motifs via `Signac::AddMotifs()`, and compute per-cell motif deviation z-scores via `Signac::RunChromVAR()`.
- We also save a copy of the object with the `"chromvar"` assay so future runs of this notebook skip `RunChromVAR()` and finish in seconds.

```{r run_chromvar}
DefaultAssay(multiome_obj) <- "ATAC"

# Fetch JASPAR2020 vertebrate CORE motifs
pfm <- getMatrixSet(
  x = JASPAR2020,
  opts = list(collection = "CORE", tax_group = "vertebrates", all_versions = FALSE)
)

# Build a lookup table mapping JASPAR Motif ID <-> TF Gene Symbol
motif_lookup <- data.frame(
  motif_id   = names(pfm),
  motif_name = vapply(pfm, function(x) name(x), character(1)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>%
  mutate(
    # Strip Secondary/Var annotations like "(var.2)" and uppercase for gene matching
    gene_symbol = toupper(sub("\\(.*\\)$", "", motif_name))
  )

# Compatibility wrapper for Signac >= 1.16.0 (where RunChromVAR was removed from Signac)
run_chromvar_compat <- function(object, genome, assay = "ATAC", new.assay.name = "chromvar") {
  if (exists("RunChromVAR", where = asNamespace("Signac"), mode = "function")) {
    Signac_RunChromVAR <- get("RunChromVAR", envir = asNamespace("Signac"))
    return(Signac_RunChromVAR(
      object         = object,
      genome         = genome,
      assay          = assay,
      new.assay.name = new.assay.name
    ))
  }
  
  cat("Signac >= 1.16.0 detected (RunChromVAR wrapper removed); running chromVAR directly...\n")
  peak_counts  <- GetAssayData(object, assay = assay, layer = "counts")
  peak_ranges  <- granges(object[[assay]])
  motif_matrix <- GetMotifData(object, assay = assay, slot = "data")
  
  # Keep peaks with > 0 total counts across cells
  keep_peaks <- Matrix::rowSums(peak_counts) > 0
  if (sum(!keep_peaks) > 0) {
    peak_counts  <- peak_counts[keep_peaks, , drop = FALSE]
    peak_ranges  <- peak_ranges[keep_peaks]
    motif_matrix <- motif_matrix[keep_peaks, , drop = FALSE]
  }
  
  chromvar_se <- SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(
    assays    = list(counts = peak_counts),
    rowRanges = peak_ranges
  )
  chromvar_se <- chromVAR::addGCBias(object = chromvar_se, genome = genome)
  bg_peaks    <- chromVAR::getBackgroundPeaks(object = chromvar_se)
  dev         <- chromVAR::computeDeviations(
    object           = chromvar_se,
    annotations      = motif_matrix,
    background_peaks = bg_peaks
  )
  
  z_mat <- chromVAR::deviationScores(dev)
  rownames(z_mat) <- colnames(motif_matrix)
  colnames(z_mat) <- colnames(object)
  z_mat[is.na(z_mat)] <- 0
  
  object[[new.assay.name]] <- Seurat::CreateAssayObject(data = z_mat)
  return(object)
}

if (!"chromvar" %in% names(multiome_obj@assays)) {
  cat("Computing JASPAR2020 motif positions and running chromVAR...\n")
  
  # Only run AddMotifs if motifs are not yet attached to the ATAC assay
  if (is.null(Motifs(multiome_obj[["ATAC"]]))) {
    # Keep standard chromosomes in BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38
    main_chroms <- standardChromosomes(BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38)
    atac_gr <- granges(multiome_obj[["ATAC"]])
    keep_peaks <- as.logical(seqnames(atac_gr) %in% main_chroms) & (width(atac_gr) > 75)
    
    if (sum(!keep_peaks) > 0) {
      cat(sprintf("Filtering ATAC assay to %d / %d standard-chromosome peaks (width > 75 bp)...\n",
                  sum(keep_peaks), length(keep_peaks)))
      multiome_obj[["ATAC"]] <- subset(multiome_obj[["ATAC"]], features = rownames(multiome_obj[["ATAC"]])[keep_peaks])
    }
    
    # Attach motif matrix
    multiome_obj <- AddMotifs(
      object = multiome_obj,
      genome = BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38,
      pfm    = pfm
    )
  } else {
    cat("Motif object already attached to ATAC assay; skipping AddMotifs().\n")
  }
  
  multiome_obj <- run_chromvar_compat(
    object = multiome_obj,
    genome = BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38,
    assay  = "ATAC"
  )
  
  # Save updated RDS with chromvar assay so you don't have to recompute it next time
  chromvar_rds_path <- file.path(output_dir, paste0(sample_id, "_multiome_merged_with_chromvar.rds"))
  cat("Saving updated Multiome object with 'chromvar' assay to:", chromvar_rds_path, "\n")
  saveRDS(multiome_obj, file = chromvar_rds_path)
} else {
  cat("'chromvar' assay already present in multiome_obj! Skipping RunChromVAR computation.\n")
}
```

## 5. Data-Driven Discovery of 10–15 Lineage-Defining TFs Across Clusters/Cell Types

In Wang et al. (*Nature* 2025, Fig. 1e & Methods p. 12), lineage-defining transcription factors were identified by intersecting differentially expressed genes per cell type with TFs present in `JASPAR2020` and evaluating their `chromVAR` motif activity.

Because the 8 fetal neocortical TFs in the paper (`PAX6`, `EMX2`, `EOMES`, `TBR1`, `MEF2C`, `MAF`, `SOX8`, `IRF8`) are specific to embryonic cortical development, this chunk automatically discovers the **10 to 15 lineage-defining TFs specific to our Ganglioglioma dataset**:
1. **Tri-Modal Candidate TF Universe:** Restricts candidate genes to human Transcription Factors present simultaneously in:
   - The RNA expression matrix (`RNA` or `SCT` assay),
   - The `EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86` genome annotation (`Annotation(multiome_obj)` for promoter TSS coordinates), and
   - The `JASPAR2020` `chromVAR` motif matrix (`rownames(multiome_obj[["chromvar"]])`).
2. **Differential Expression Across Cell Types/Clusters (`FindAllMarkers`):** Identifies TFs significantly upregulated (`only.pos = TRUE`, `p_val_adj < 0.05`) in each cell type/cluster (`ScType`, `Azimuth_cellType`, or `seurat_clusters`).
3. **Concordant `chromVAR` Motif Activity:** Computes the mean `chromVAR` motif deviation z-score (`mean_chromvar_z`) for each candidate TF in each cell type, prioritizing TFs with both strong differential RNA expression (`avg_log2FC`) and positive motif accessibility (`mean_chromvar_z > 0`).
4. **Balanced Top 10–15 Selection & Diagonal Ordering:** Selects the top 1–3 TFs per cluster/cell type via round-robin ranking to yield `target_n_tfs` (10–15) unique TFs, ordered by their peak cell type (`celltype_levels`) so the 3-panel plot forms a clean diagonal cascade. The full table of differentially expressed TFs is also saved to `<sample_id>_differential_lineage_TFs.csv`.

```{r discover_and_match_tfs}
# Determine RNA expression assay ("SCT" or "RNA")
rna_assay <- if ("SCT" %in% names(multiome_obj@assays)) "SCT" else "RNA"
rna_genes <- rownames(multiome_obj[[rna_assay]])
annot_genes <- unique(Annotation(multiome_obj)$gene_name)
chromvar_motifs <- rownames(multiome_obj[["chromvar"]])

# Build the universe of candidate TFs present across all 3 modalities (RNA + ATAC TSS + JASPAR2020 Motif)
candidate_tf_map <- motif_lookup %>%
  filter(
    gene_symbol %in% rna_genes,
    gene_symbol %in% annot_genes,
    motif_id %in% chromvar_motifs
  ) %>%
  group_by(gene_symbol) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup()

cat(sprintf(
  "Found %d candidate JASPAR2020 Transcription Factors present in RNA (%s), ATAC gene annotations, and chromVAR.\n",
  nrow(candidate_tf_map), rna_assay
))

if (isTRUE(auto_discover_tfs)) {
  cat("Running differential expression (FindAllMarkers) across ", celltype_col,
      " to discover the top ", min_target_tfs, "-", max_target_tfs, " lineage-defining TFs...\n", sep = "")
  
  DefaultAssay(multiome_obj) <- rna_assay
  Idents(multiome_obj) <- factor(Idents(multiome_obj), levels = celltype_levels)
  
  # If using Seurat v5 Assay5 with multiple split layers, join layers before FindAllMarkers
  if (rna_assay == "RNA" && inherits(multiome_obj[["RNA"]], "Assay5") && length(Layers(multiome_obj[["RNA"]])) > 1) {
    multiome_obj[["RNA"]] <- JoinLayers(multiome_obj[["RNA"]])
  }
  
  # 1. Run differential expression restricted to candidate TFs
  de_tfs <- FindAllMarkers(
    object          = multiome_obj,
    assay           = rna_assay,
    features        = candidate_tf_map$gene_symbol,
    only.pos        = TRUE,
    min.pct         = 0.05,
    logfc.threshold = 0.15,
    verbose         = FALSE
  )
  
  if (nrow(de_tfs) == 0) {
    warning("No differentially expressed TFs passed thresholds; falling back to manual_signature_tfs.")
    signature_tfs <- manual_signature_tfs
  } else {
    # 2. Compute per-cluster mean chromVAR z-score for every candidate TF motif
    chromvar_all <- GetAssayData(
      multiome_obj,
      assay = "chromvar",
      layer = "data"
    )[candidate_tf_map$motif_id, , drop = FALSE]
    
    cluster_vec <- as.character(Idents(multiome_obj))
    chromvar_cluster_means <- lapply(celltype_levels, function(cl) {
      cells_cl <- which(cluster_vec == cl)
      if (length(cells_cl) == 0) return(NULL)
      row_means <- Matrix::rowMeans(chromvar_all[, cells_cl, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
      data.frame(
        cluster         = cl,
        motif_id        = names(row_means),
        mean_chromvar_z = as.numeric(row_means),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    }) %>% bind_rows()
    
    # 3. Annotate DE TFs with JASPAR motif ID and cluster-specific chromVAR activity
    de_tfs_annotated <- de_tfs %>%
      inner_join(candidate_tf_map, by = c("gene" = "gene_symbol")) %>%
      left_join(
        chromvar_cluster_means,
        by = c("cluster" = "cluster", "motif_id" = "motif_id")
      ) %>%
      mutate(
        cluster = factor(as.character(cluster), levels = celltype_levels),
        concordant_motif = !is.na(mean_chromvar_z) & (mean_chromvar_z > 0)
      ) %>%
      arrange(cluster, desc(concordant_motif), desc(avg_log2FC), p_val_adj)
    
    # Export full differential TF table to CSV
    de_csv_path <- file.path(output_dir, paste0(sample_id, "_differential_lineage_TFs.csv"))
    write.csv(de_tfs_annotated, file = de_csv_path, row.names = FALSE)
    cat("Saved full differential TF table (", nrow(de_tfs_annotated), " entries) to: ", de_csv_path, "\n", sep = "")
    
    # Filter to statistically significant markers (p_val_adj < 0.05; fallback to p_val < 0.05 if needed)
    sig_de_tfs <- de_tfs_annotated %>% filter(p_val_adj < 0.05)
    if ( length(unique(sig_de_tfs$gene)) < min_target_tfs ) {
      sig_de_tfs <- de_tfs_annotated %>% filter(p_val < 0.05)
    }
    
    # Assign cluster rank per TF within each cell type
    ranked_per_cluster <- sig_de_tfs %>%
      group_by(cluster) %>%
      mutate(rank_in_cluster = row_number()) %>%
      ungroup() %>%
      arrange(rank_in_cluster, cluster, desc(avg_log2FC))
    
    # Round-robin selection across clusters (rank 1 per cluster first, then rank 2, 3...)
    # to select target_n_tfs (bounded between min_target_tfs and max_target_tfs)
    n_goal <- min(max(target_n_tfs, min_target_tfs), max_target_tfs)
    selected_rows <- list()
    seen_genes <- character(0)
    
    for (r in seq_len(max(ranked_per_cluster$rank_in_cluster, na.rm = TRUE))) {
      sub_r <- ranked_per_cluster %>% filter(rank_in_cluster == r)
      for (i in seq_len(nrow(sub_r))) {
        g <- sub_r$gene[i]
        if (!g %in% seen_genes) {
          seen_genes <- c(seen_genes, g)
          selected_rows[[length(selected_rows) + 1]] <- sub_r[i, , drop = FALSE]
        }
        if (length(seen_genes) >= n_goal) break
      }
      if (length(seen_genes) >= n_goal) break
    }
    
    selected_tf_df <- bind_rows(selected_rows) %>%
      mutate(cluster = factor(as.character(cluster), levels = celltype_levels)) %>%
      arrange(cluster, rank_in_cluster, desc(avg_log2FC))
    
    signature_tfs <- as.character(selected_tf_df$gene)
    cat(sprintf(
      "Auto-discovered %d lineage-defining TFs across %d cell types/clusters:\n  %s\n",
      length(signature_tfs),
      length(unique(selected_tf_df$cluster)),
      paste(signature_tfs, collapse = ", ")
    ))
  }
} else {
  signature_tfs <- manual_signature_tfs
  cat("Using manual signature TFs:\n  ", paste(signature_tfs, collapse = ", "), "\n")
}

# Map final signature TFs to their JASPAR motif IDs
tf_map <- candidate_tf_map %>%
  filter(gene_symbol %in% signature_tfs)

valid_tfs <- signature_tfs[signature_tfs %in% tf_map$gene_symbol]
missing_tfs <- setdiff(signature_tfs, valid_tfs)
if (length(missing_tfs) > 0) {
  message("Note: The following TFs were missing from one of the modalities and skipped: ",
          paste(missing_tfs, collapse = ", "))
}
if (length(valid_tfs) == 0) {
  stop("No signature TFs matched across RNA, ATAC annotations, and JASPAR2020 chromVAR motifs!")
}

tf_map <- tf_map %>%
  filter(gene_symbol %in% valid_tfs) %>%
  mutate(gene_symbol = factor(gene_symbol, levels = valid_tfs)) %>%
  arrange(gene_symbol)

if (exists("selected_tf_df") && nrow(selected_tf_df) > 0) {
  display_df <- selected_tf_df %>%
    select(
      Peak_Cluster = cluster,
      TF_Gene      = gene,
      JASPAR_Motif = motif_id,
      avg_log2FC,
      pct.1,
      pct.2,
      p_val_adj,
      mean_chromvar_z
    )
  knitr::kable(
    display_df,
    digits  = 3,
    caption = paste0("Top ", nrow(display_df), " Data-Driven Lineage-Defining TFs Discovered Across ", celltype_col)
  )
} else {
  knitr::kable(tf_map, caption = "Validated Signature TFs & Corresponding JASPAR2020 Motif IDs")
}
```

---

## 6. Panel 1 (Left): Gene Expression Dot Plot (`Fraction of cells` & `Min-Max Normalized Mean Expression`)

In Figure 1e (left panel):
- **Rows:** Cell types (`celltype_levels`, ordered top-to-bottom).
- **Columns:** Signature TFs (`valid_tfs`, labels placed at the top and rotated 90°).
- **Dot Size:** Percentage of cells within the cell type expressing the TF (`pct_exp > 0`).
- **Dot Fill Color:** Mean normalized RNA expression in each cell type, **min–max scaled to `[0, 1]`** across cell types for each TF using the `viridis` palette.

```{r panel1_gene_expression, fig.width=5, fig.height=8}
DefaultAssay(multiome_obj) <- rna_assay
expr_mat <- GetAssayData(multiome_obj, assay = rna_assay, layer = "data")[valid_tfs, , drop = FALSE]

# Compute per-cell-type mean expression and % expressing cells
cell_groups <- Idents(multiome_obj)

gex_summary <- lapply(valid_tfs, function(tf) {
  vals <- as.numeric(expr_mat[tf, ])
  df <- data.frame(
    cell_type = cell_groups,
    expr      = vals
  ) %>%
    group_by(cell_type) %>%
    summarise(
      mean_expr = mean(expr, na.rm = TRUE),
      pct_exp   = mean(expr > 0, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
      .groups   = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      tf = tf,
      # Min-max normalize [0, 1] across cell types for this TF (as in Fig. 1e)
      norm_expr = if (max(mean_expr) > min(mean_expr)) {
        (mean_expr - min(mean_expr)) / (max(mean_expr) - min(mean_expr))
      } else {
        0
      }
    )
  df
}) %>% bind_rows()

# Lock factor levels so top-to-bottom row order matches across all 3 panels
gex_summary$cell_type <- factor(gex_summary$cell_type, levels = rev(celltype_levels))
gex_summary$tf <- factor(gex_summary$tf, levels = valid_tfs)

p_panel1_gex <- ggplot(gex_summary, aes(x = tf, y = cell_type)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = pct_exp, fill = norm_expr), shape = 21, color = "black", stroke = 0.4) +
  scale_size_continuous(
    name   = "Fraction of cells\nin group (%)",
    range  = c(0.5, 5.5),
    limits = c(0, 100),
    breaks = c(20, 40, 60, 80, 100)
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    name   = "Mean expression\nin group",
    option = "viridis",
    limits = c(0, 1),
    breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1.0)
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  labs(title = "Gene expression", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title        = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 12),
    axis.text.x.top   = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 0, vjust = 0.5, face = "italic", color = "black"),
    axis.text.y       = element_text(color = "black", size = 10),
    panel.grid.major  = element_line(color = "grey92", linewidth = 0.3),
    legend.position   = "bottom",
    legend.box        = "horizontal",
    legend.title      = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.text       = element_text(size = 7),
    plot.margin       = margin(5, 2, 5, 5)
  )

print(p_panel1_gex)
```

---

## 7. Panel 2 (Middle): Promoter Chromatin Accessibility Coverage Tracks (`Signac::CoveragePlot`)

In Figure 1e (middle panel):
- For each signature TF, we locate its **canonical Transcription Start Site (TSS / promoter region)** in `Annotation(multiome_obj)` and extend by `+/- promoter_flank_bp` (default $\pm 1,500\text{ bp}$).
- We use `Signac::CoveragePlot()` to plot aggregated ATAC-seq insertion coverage across all cell types (in the exact `celltype_levels` order) with the gene TSS model underneath.

```{r panel2_promoter_accessibility, fig.width=12, fig.height=8}
DefaultAssay(multiome_obj) <- "ATAC"
Idents(multiome_obj) <- factor(Idents(multiome_obj), levels = celltype_levels)

# Helper function to compute the promoter GRanges window around a gene's TSS
get_promoter_region <- function(gene_symbol, annot_gr, flank_bp = 1500) {
  gene_sub <- annot_gr[!is.na(annot_gr$gene_name) & annot_gr$gene_name == gene_symbol]
  if (length(gene_sub) == 0) return(gene_symbol)
  
  # Collapse gene span and determine canonical 5' TSS coordinate
  strand_val <- as.character(strand(gene_sub)[1])
  chr_val    <- as.character(seqnames(gene_sub)[1])
  tss_coord  <- if (strand_val == "-") max(end(gene_sub)) else min(start(gene_sub))
  
   sprintf("%s-%d-%d", chr_val, max(1, tss_coord - flank_bp), tss_coord + flank_bp)
}

annot_gr <- Annotation(multiome_obj)

# Generate a distinct palette matching the number of cell types
n_types <- length(celltype_levels)
type_palette <- scales::hue_pal()(n_types)
names(type_palette) <- celltype_levels

cov_plot_list <- lapply(seq_along(valid_tfs), function(idx) {
  tf <- valid_tfs[idx]
  promoter_region <- get_promoter_region(tf, annot_gr, flank_bp = promoter_flank_bp)
  
  p_cov <- CoveragePlot(
    object             = multiome_obj,
    region             = promoter_region,
    annotation         = TRUE,
    peaks              = FALSE,
    links              = FALSE,
    group.by           = celltype_col,
     idents             = celltype_levels,
    heights            = c(10, 1.5)
  ) &
    scale_fill_manual(values = type_palette) &
    theme(
      legend.position  = "none",
      axis.title.x     = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x      = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x     = element_blank(),
      axis.title.y     = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y      = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y     = element_blank(),
      strip.text.y.left = element_blank(),
      plot.margin      = margin(2, 1, 2, 1)
    )
  
  # Add the TF title at the top of each column track
  p_cov[[1]] <- p_cov[[1]] +
    ggtitle(tf) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10, face = "italic"))
  
  p_cov
})

p_panel2_atac <- wrap_plots(cov_plot_list, ncol = length(cov_plot_list)) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Chromatin accessibility",
    theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 12))
  )

print(p_panel2_atac)
```

---

## 8. Panel 3 (Right): Normalized `chromVAR` Motif Activity Heatmap

In Figure 1e (right panel) and the paper's Methods (*"TF motif enrichment analysis"*, p. 12):
- For each signature TF's JASPAR2020 motif, we average the per-cell `chromVAR` deviation z-scores within each cell type.
- We then apply **min–max normalization (`[0, 1]`)** across cell types for each motif (`Normalized chromVAR activity`) and plot a `geom_tile()` heatmap using the `viridis` palette.

```{r panel3_motif_activity, fig.width=4.5, fig.height=8}
DefaultAssay(multiome_obj) <- "chromvar"
chromvar_mat <- GetAssayData(multiome_obj, assay = "chromvar", layer = "data")[tf_map$motif_id, , drop = FALSE]

motif_summary <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(tf_map)), function(i) {
  tf_sym   <- as.character(tf_map$gene_symbol[i])
  motif_id <- tf_map$motif_id[i]
  vals     <- as.numeric(chromvar_mat[motif_id, ])
  
  df <- data.frame(
    cell_type = Idents(multiome_obj),
    score     = vals
  ) %>%
    group_by(cell_type) %>%
    summarise(
      mean_chromvar = mean(score, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups       = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      tf = tf_sym,
      # Min-max normalize [0, 1] across cell types for this TF motif
      norm_chromvar = if (max(mean_chromvar, na.rm = TRUE) > min(mean_chromvar, na.rm = TRUE)) {
        (mean_chromvar - min(mean_chromvar, na.rm = TRUE)) /
          (max(mean_chromvar, na.rm = TRUE) - min(mean_chromvar, na.rm = TRUE))
      } else {
        0
      }
    )
  df
}) %>% bind_rows()

motif_summary$cell_type <- factor(motif_summary$cell_type, levels = rev(celltype_levels))
motif_summary$tf <- factor(motif_summary$tf, levels = valid_tfs)

p_panel3_motif <- ggplot(motif_summary, aes(x = tf, y = cell_type, fill = norm_chromvar)) +
  geom_tile(color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.25) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    name   = "Normalized\nchromVAR activity",
    option = "viridis",
    limits = c(0, 1),
    breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1.0)
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  labs(title = "Motif activity", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 12),
    axis.text.x.top  = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 0, vjust = 0.5, face = "italic", color = "black"),
    axis.text.y      = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y     = element_blank(),
    panel.grid       = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    legend.title     = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.text      = element_text(size = 7),
    plot.margin      = margin(5, 5, 5, 2)
  )

print(p_panel3_motif)
```

---

## 9. Assemble & Export Complete 3-Panel Figure 1E

We align **Panel 1 (Gene Expression)**, **Panel 2 (Promoter Chromatin Accessibility)**, and **Panel 3 (`chromVAR` Motif Activity)** side-by-side and save both PDF and PNG versions in `output_dir`.

```{r assemble_figure1e, fig.width=18, fig.height=10}
# Combine the 3 panels horizontally with proportional widths matching Figure 1e
fig1e_combined <- (p_panel1_gex | wrap_plots(cov_plot_list, ncol = length(cov_plot_list)) | p_panel3_motif) +
  plot_layout(widths = c(1.5, 4.2, 1.3)) +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = paste0(sample_id, " - Tri-Modal Signature TF Validation (Gene Expression, Promoter Accessibility & Motif Activity)"),
    subtitle = paste0("Grouped by: ", celltype_col, " (n = ", ncol(multiome_obj), " cells)"),
    theme    = theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 14),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 11)
    )
  )

print(fig1e_combined)

# Save high-resolution PDF and PNG
fig1e_pdf <- file.path(output_dir, paste0(sample_id, "_Figure1E_trimodal_TF_validation.pdf"))
fig1e_png <- file.path(output_dir, paste0(sample_id, "_Figure1E_trimodal_TF_validation.png"))

ggsave(filename = fig1e_pdf, plot = fig1e_combined, width = 18, height = 10, units = "in")
ggsave(filename = fig1e_png, plot = fig1e_combined, width = 18, height = 10, units = "in", dpi = 300)

cat("Saved Figure 1E PDF to:", fig1e_pdf, "\n")
cat("Saved Figure 1E PNG to:", fig1e_png, "\n")
```
